definition: The ability of an element to form compounds in which it has two or more different oxidation states, as iron does in $\ce{FeCl2}$ and $\ce{FeCl3}$. Transition elements show it because their 4s and 3d electrons are close in energy, so successive ionization energies rise without a large jump.
A central metal ion bonded to a number of ligands by coordination bonds, written in square brackets with its overall charge, such as $\ce{[Ni(H2O)6]^2+}$.
A molecule or ion, such as $\ce{H2O}$, $\ce{NH3}$ or $\ce{Cl^-}$, that donates a lone pair of electrons to a central metal ion to form a coordination bond; a ligand is a Lewis base.
